Napoleon Bonaparte waits beside a table covered in maps. A survey of the Nile's wells has vanished; soldiers and villages alike depend on finding it.
Salma waits beneath a striped awning. The cartographer recognises a mark on the abandoned map case: the thief left through the harbour.
Mooring ropes creak among the cargo bales. A smuggler is keeping curious eyes away from a crate bearing the expedition's seal.
Follow the path along the quay
Lucien Morel asks why one receipt lists the same boat twice. A splash of ink hides the recipient's name.
A shadow closes a crate behind a row of jars. You can follow the porters through their passage or challenge the armed lookout.
Follow the porters through the passage
Salma waits beside an open window. She has found the name of a ferryman who knows the canals better than the officers do.
Climb through the window towards the canal
Youssef waits beside his damaged boat. Someone has cut the mooring lines; an armed man now claims the right to collect a crossing fee.
Talk to Youssef about another boat
The pilot draws the river channels on a damp stone. The route to Rosetta remains open if you leave before the supply convoy.
Examine the drawing on the stone
The wind drives salt against your boots. An irregular guard blocks the direct road, but workers use a raised walkway to the side.
Climb the ladder to the walkway
Youssef waits beneath a blue sail. He will take you to the first lock if you help him prepare the boat.
A lantern still burns in the empty watchpost. Its returning lookout wants the notebook you spotted, but he may listen to an explanation.
Talk to the lookout about passing through
Three carved lines indicate a channel towards cultivated fields. Salma recognises a surveying method used by an expedition engineer.
Grain sacks form a quiet maze. A marauder guards a hidden cache; local residents show you a way out towards the market.
Follow the path towards the market
Amina asks for news of the convoy. She saw a man carrying the stolen case as though it held a treasure.
The bookbinder repaired a sand-covered notebook. A torn page shows a small dam and an officer's initials.
The river turns orange at sunset. Youssef warns that the next stage will take you along the banks and into the irrigation canals.
Board the boat beside the Nile
A narrow track winds between the reeds. The sound of an oar lets you follow another boat without approaching it.
A motionless wheel holds debris from a flood. One part of its mechanism resembles the sketch in the stolen notebook.
Amina waits beside a cooled kiln. The potters carried jars for men who spoke of a concealed cistern.
Talk to Amina by the kiln
Salma studies the palm shadows. She concludes that the notebook's drawing was made in an east-facing courtyard.
Look across the river through the telescope
A deserter guards a chest of military papers. The supply officer knows a path around his post.
The doctor asks you to conserve drinking water. A wounded courier heard the name of a village where the maps are to change hands.
General Desaix waits outside an open tent. He grants you passage through the lines without diverting soldiers from their duties.
A gardener closes the little sluices one by one. His account confirms that a side canal reaches the village you seek.
Stone steps descend beneath the palms. Red sealing wax clings to the last dry step.
Descend the stairs to the boat
Youssef waits for the ferry. Across the river, two routes lead to a caravanserai without entering the military camp.
Salma asks travellers about a case marked with a compass. A merchant recognises it and points towards the inner courtyard.
Talk to Salma in the courtyard
An open window overlooks the rooftops. Beneath a rolled carpet lies a draft survey describing the flow of several wells.
Examine the survey beneath the carpet
A trafficker watches the stairs to discourage pursuit. A mason's ladder offers another way around his post.
The baker recognises the stamp on the survey. His neighbour engraves merchants' seals and is still working despite the heat.
Follow the path to the workshop
Farid asks to see the wax impression. A tiny notch identifies a forged seal used to divert supply convoys.
Stars shimmer in the rooftop pools. Salma connects the clues: the maps are being used to sell false access to water reserves.
Watch the stars before setting out
News of the army catches up with you. You must reach the quartermasters before another convoy follows a false map.
Officers arrange cloth squares on a table to explain their movements. A messenger tells you where Bonaparte will be after the council.
Napoleon Bonaparte waits for a precise report. He wants evidence of the diversions and leaves you to decide how to protect the civilian convoy.
The distant noise of battle unsettles the porters. Your task is to guide civilians through a sheltered passage, away from the fighting.
Follow the passage behind the embankment
An armed man is moving supplies under cover of the confusion. Salma suggests asking the storekeeper for help instead of confronting him.
Talk to the storekeeper about protecting the supplies
Amina waits beside a well with a broken rope. The carpenters can help restore the crossing used by the families.
Take the path to the carpenters
The carpenters assemble salvaged planks. They saw a man carrying the map case towards the river.
Youssef has found a light boat. The fugitives followed the channel beside the ruins of an old quay.
Broken columns rise from the sand. A fresh chalk message arranges a meeting near Cairo.
Salma speaks with a neighbourhood official. He will help if the inquiry is not used as an excuse to seize the residents' water.
Talk to Salma and the official
Water runs between stone basins. Farid finds the same forged seal on a jar that he saw on the notebook.
Examine the jar with the forged seal
A copyist keeps duplicates of transport contracts. A page was removed so recently that the ink on its neighbour is still damp.
An accomplice returns for the last contract. The copyist shows you a hiding place where you can let him pass and then read the papers.
Gaspard Monge waits beside an incomplete survey. He confirms that the notebook combines useful measurements with deliberately false directions.
The scholars arrange their instruments on a table. Salma proposes comparing the notebook's bearings with the plain of Giza.
Youssef waits on the western bank. Beyond the fields and palms, the pyramids finally emerge from the dust.
Salma examines a survey marker. The stolen sketch indicates a cistern near the ancient paths, not a secret chamber inside a pyramid.
Wind whistles between the columns. Part of a map case protrudes from the sand beside a recently disturbed step.
Farid waits with two workers who maintain the water access routes. They saw the suspects descend to a storehouse away from the monuments.
Talk to Farid and the workers
A service gallery shelters the water jars from the sun. Fresh tracks stop at a wooden door secured from within.
The leader of the scheme guards the last notebook. Salma wants to negotiate its return while the workers secure the path to the well.
Talk to the keeper about returning the notebook
The complete plan lies on a low table. You can correct the false directions once you identify which measurements are trustworthy.
Examine the map beside the cistern
Salma compares the shadows with Monge's measurements. The true water route reaches a village the convoy had not planned to serve.
Observe the shadows through the telescope
Amina waits in the square. The residents ask to receive corrected maps at the same time as the army.
Talk to Amina in the square
The copyist spreads sheets across a table. You prepare two clear copies so that no group depends on a single precious original.
Youssef packs the documents into a watertight chest. You cross back to camp carrying the villagers' testimony.
Board the boat carrying the documents
Napoleon Bonaparte waits with the quartermasters. Your report separates established facts from the rumours that surrounded the investigation.
Talk to Napoleon Bonaparte at the council
Salma asks for the water access arrangements in writing. An officer agrees to deliver a copy to the village before the convoy leaves.
Examine the agreement on the table
An accomplice still wants the forged seal. Farid proposes handing it to the neighbourhood officials with the evidence of the scheme.
Talk to Farid about handing over the evidence
The first convoy follows the corrected route. You accompany the porters as far as the branch leading to the village.
The sun sinks behind the palms and pyramids. Salma joins you to decide who should keep the last field notebook.
Two tasks await: accompany the scholars on their surveys, or help the residents maintain their water routes. Bonaparte has his maps; your own road is yours to choose.
Give the notebook to the scholars
